traits: Entirely hollow, very thin trumpet, rarely over 10 cm, with a widely wavy, scalloped margin
Inside covered in scales, grey-black to dark brown depending on moisture
Outer face almost smooth, light to dark grey: no gills, no pores
Hollow stem, the colour of the cap, tapering to the base
Pleasant fruity smell (mirabelle plum) · white spores
Broadleaf woods (beech, oak, chestnut), in groups, heavy damp soils · August to November
safetyNote: The outer face is smooth: no gills. A very old, blackened russula has a convex cap and broad gills; the worthless charcoal-burner’s false chanterelle has forked gills and grows only on burnt ground. Wild mushrooms are prepared within 24 hours.
